findings.description: collect_problems() documents 'return every configuration problem instead of raising', but _schema_problems() calls _load_schema(), which raises OwnershipConfigError('invalid_map', 'owners.schema.json is not installed') when neither the install_assets copy nor openspec/schemas/ exists; the exception escapes collect_problems() and so check_owners.check() / codeowners.reconcile() crash with a traceback instead of emitting an invalid_map finding. Likewise read_codeowners() does path.read_bytes().decode('utf-8') unguarded, so an unreadable or non-UTF-8 .github/CODEOWNERS raises OSError/UnicodeDecodeError out of reconcile() rather than producing a finding. Both are on the file-I/O failure path this module is meant to guard (principals.read_registry wraps the equivalent read in OSError handling).
findings.existing_code:
def _schema_problems(raw: Any, repo_root: Path) -> list[Problem]:
    validator = Draft202012Validator(_load_schema(repo_root))
findings.resolution: Catch OwnershipConfigError around _load_schema in _schema_problems (or in collect_problems) and return it as a Problem; wrap read_codeowners' read/decode in try/except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) and surface a codeowners finding.

findings.description: The Ownership Check requirement states SHALL-level behaviour for two warnings that have no WHEN/THEN scenario: 'every item in any active roadmap.yaml with no explicit assignment' (unowned_roadmap_item) and 'a solo principal that is the sentinel' (sentinel_principal). Only unowned_capability and unknown_capability have scenarios; the roadmap and sentinel halves are covered by tests (test_unowned_roadmap_item_reported, test_sentinel_principal_warning) but not by the normative spec, so the spec-to-scenario rule for this group is not met for those clauses.
findings.resolution: Add scenarios 'Unowned roadmap item reported' (team mode) and 'Sentinel principal reported' mirroring the existing tests.

findings.description: Spec Solo Mode says the sole principal is derived as: single declared human; else `git:<email>` from git config user.email; else the `repository-default` sentinel. derive_solo_principal() inserts an extra step: when user.email is unset but user.name is set it returns Principal(id='git:<name>', source='git-config'). Design D5 mentions '(then user.name)', so the design and code agree, but the spec requirement and the 'Sentinel when no identity is available' scenario do not describe this id shape; a downstream consumer reading the spec would not expect a `git:` id that is not an email.
findings.existing_code:
if name:
            return Principal(id=f"git:{name}", display_name=name, source="git-config")
findings.resolution: Either state the user.name fallback in the spec Solo Mode requirement or drop it and fall straight to the sentinel.

findings.description: active_roadmap_items() silently `continue`s when an active roadmap.yaml cannot be read or parsed. In that case every roadmap_items assignment for that roadmap is reported as unknown_roadmap_item ('is in no active roadmap') and, in team mode, no unowned_roadmap_item findings are emitted for it, so a corrupt roadmap file is misreported as a map typo and nothing names the real cause.
findings.resolution: Emit a warning finding (e.g. a new code or reuse unknown_roadmap_item with a message naming the unreadable file) instead of swallowing the error, or at least log it in the message of the resulting unknown_roadmap_item findings.

findings.description: Two definitions of 'literal prefix' exist: Rule.literal_length (owners.py) counts a leading '/' in the pattern, while codeowners._literal_prefix strips it with lstrip('/') before locating the first metacharacter. Resolution and emit both use Rule.sort_key so they stay consistent with each other, but '/openspec/x' and 'openspec/x' (identical semantics per D3) get different specificity, and the reconcile probe prefix is computed by a different function than the one that ranks rules. Harmless today; a maintenance trap if either is changed alone.
findings.resolution: Have Rule expose literal_prefix and derive both literal_length and the probe prefix from it (strip the leading '/' in one place).

findings.description: check_owners.check(codeowners=True) builds the context via collect_problems() and then codeowners.check_findings() -> reconcile() calls collect_problems() again, re-reading and re-validating owners.yaml and the registry (including the shipped-schema JSON loads) a second time in the same run. On disagreement the resolver is also invoked twice per probe (_expected_handles and again for matched_rule). Within the 250 ms design budget today, but doubles the I/O for every CI run of the invariant.
findings.resolution: Let reconcile() accept an already-built OwnershipContext (check_findings already has ctx in hand) and resolve each probe once.

findings.description: Re-verification of open ledger item 6: PathPattern in all three schema copies still admits an embedded `**` and `***`; compile_pattern() in owners.py rejects it with invalid_map and the fixture embedded_double_star_schema_ok.json documents the split. Two-layer validation remains as designed in D3; no change.

Re-verification of open ledger item 12: _strings / _strings_in in the two coordinator tests still use exact string equality against the human id, and the negative tests inject only a bare 'jan' row. A composite projection string (agent:jan, agents/jan/...) would still pass undetected. Status unchanged; the session log records why substring matching was rejected (false positives on unrelated 'jan' substrings).

Re-verification of open ledger item 13: test_adding_a_capability_directory_causes_no_unowned_churn still asserts report['findings'] == [] and then asserts no code starts with 'unowned_'; the second assertion remains vacuous. Status unchanged.
